correctness.rationale: An odd circular length exchanges vertex parity and a length-two edge preserves it, so the counts of even-even and odd-odd edges are equal. If 3 divides n, each residue class modulo 3 initially has even size and length-three edges remain within it, so a single length-one edge with no length twos makes two classes impossible to finish. Each of the six displayed blocks covers its interval with the specified ordinary differences, which are also the circular lengths because 3<=n. For b>0 even, use b/2-1 pure length-two blocks, triples of length threes, singles of length one, and a residue block consuming the final two length twos with zero, one or two length threes. For b=0 and c=3q+r, pair each residual length three with a length one if a>=r. The remaining a<r cases are the pure length-three cycle (the map from even labels to odd labels by +3 mod 2n is a bijection) and a=1,r=2, precisely the obstruction. This includes n=3 and proves the equivalence for arbitrary n, independently of the tests. A definition-based independent matching recursion reproduced every profile for 3<=n<=10, with counts 5,9,12,15,20,25,29,36; these finite checks corroborate rather than prove the infinite statement.
residual_risks: Neither the proof nor the checks classify multisets including longer distances or count the matchings of a given profile.
